passage:
Researchers built a boat using ancient methods to test whether people could have traveled between islands long ago.
The boat was not just a display. It was sailed on real water under controlled conditions.
Students followed the project online. They learned that experimental archaeology tests possibilities by doing, not only by imagining.
The boat trip was difficult. Weather, waves, and materials all mattered.
The experiment did not prove every detail of ancient travel, but it showed what might have been possible.
Sometimes studying history means rebuilding a tool and letting wind, water, and human skill answer part of the question.
